Name: Abacus
Description: A standard tool used by merchants and scribes to calculate complex sums rapidly.
Usage Implications: Assists in tracking large sums of currency, trade goods, or complex mathematical calculations.

Name: Acid (vial)
Description: A small glass vial filled with highly corrosive liquid.
Usage Implications: Can be thrown as an improvised weapon (range 20/60 ft). On a hit, deals 2d6 acid damage.

Name: Alchemist's Fire (flask)
Description: A sticky, volatile adhesive fluid that ignites when exposed to air.
Usage Implications: Thrown as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1d4 fire damage at the start of each of its turns until an action is used to extinguish the flames.

Name: Antitoxin (vial)
Description: A specially brewed liquid that purges toxins from the bloodstream.
Usage Implications: Drinking it grants advantage on saving throws against poison for 1 hour.

Name: Backpack
Description: A sturdy canvas or leather pack designed to distribute weight across the shoulders and back.
Usage Implications: Can hold 1 cubic foot or 30 pounds of gear. You can strap items like bedrolls or rope to the outside.

Name: Ball Bearings (bag of 1,000)
Description: A small pouch containing hundreds of tiny metal spheres.
Usage Implications: As an action, cover a 10-foot-square area. Creatures moving through it must succeed on a DC 10 Dexterity saving throw or fall prone.

Name: Bedroll
Description: Thick blankets and a ground pad designed to provide minimal comfort while sleeping outdoors.
Usage Implications: Required to properly benefit from a long rest in outdoor or dungeon environments without incurring exhaustion from exposure.

Name: Bell
Description: A simple brass bell without a handle.
Usage Implications: Used for signaling, rigging simple alarms with string, or drawing attention.

Name: Block and Tackle
Description: A set of pulleys and rope used to hoist heavy objects.
Usage Implications: Allows you to hoist up to four times the weight you can normally lift.

Name: Bullseye Lantern
Description: A brass lantern with a reflective back and a curved glass lens to focus light into a beam.
Usage Implications: Burns for 6 hours on a flask of oil. Casts bright light in a 60-foot cone and dim light for an additional 60 feet.

Name: Caltrops (bag of 20)
Description: Four-pronged metal spikes designed so one prong always faces upward.
Usage Implications: Cover a 5-foot-square area. Creatures entering the area must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity save or stop moving and take 1 piercing damage, reducing their walking speed by 10 feet until healed.

Name: Climber's Kit
Description: Special pitons, boot tips, gloves, and a harness.
Usage Implications: Using it as an action secures you to the wall, preventing falls of more than 25 feet. Does not grant a climb speed.

Name: Crowbar
Description: A heavy iron bar with a wedged end used for prying.
Usage Implications: Grants advantage on Strength checks where the crowbar's leverage can be applied.

Name: Grappling Hook
Description: A multi-pronged iron hook designed to catch on ledges or branches.
Usage Implications: Can be attached to a rope to secure a climbing path. Requires an attack roll or ability check to lodge securely into a target surface.

Name: Healer's Kit
Description: A leather pouch containing bandages, salves, and splints.
Usage Implications: Has 10 uses. As an action, expend one use to stabilize a dying creature without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check.

Name: Hooded Lantern
Description: A standard oil lantern with a deployable metal hood to restrict light.
Usage Implications: Burns for 6 hours. Casts 30 ft bright light and 30 ft dim light. Using an action to lower the hood reduces the light to dim light in a 5-foot radius.

Name: Hunting Trap
Description: A heavy iron jaw trap secured by a heavy chain to a stationary object.
Usage Implications: DC 13 Dex save to avoid. On fail, creature takes 1d4 piercing damage and is stopped. Escaping requires a DC 13 Strength check.

Name: Lock
Description: A heavy padlock that comes with a key.
Usage Implications: Can be picked with thieves' tools. The DC depends on the quality of the lock, usually requiring a DC 15 Dexterity check for a standard lock.

Name: Magnifying Glass
Description: A lens crafted to enlarge small details.
Usage Implications: Grants advantage on ability checks made to appraise or inspect small or highly detailed items. Can also start a fire with sunlight and tinder in 5 minutes.

Name: Manacles
Description: Metal restraints meant to bind a Small or Medium creature.
Usage Implications: Requires a DC 20 Dexterity check to slip out of, or a DC 20 Strength check to break them. Has 15 hit points.

Name: Oil (flask)
Description: Refined fuel for lamps, or a highly flammable hazard.
Usage Implications: Can be splashed on a creature (ranged attack). If the target takes fire damage before the oil dries (1 minute), it takes an additional 5 fire damage.

Name: Poison, Basic (vial)
Description: A rudimentary toxic paste derived from common venomous creatures or plants.
Usage Implications: Applied to a weapon or 3 pieces of ammunition. Next target hit must make a DC 10 Con save or take 1d4 poison damage. Remains potent for 1 minute.

Name: Rations (1 day)
Description: Compact, dry foods such as jerky, hardtack, dried fruit, and nuts.
Usage Implications: Prevents exhaustion from starvation. One ration sustains a standard humanoid for one day.

Name: Rope, Hempen (50 feet)
Description: A thick, heavy, woven rope made of natural plant fibers.
Usage Implications: Has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

Name: Rope, Silk (50 feet)
Description: An expensive, lightweight rope prized for its strength and flexibility.
Usage Implications: Has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check. Weighs significantly less than hempen rope.

Name: Thieves' Tools
Description: A specialized set containing files, lock picks, a small mirror mounted on a metal handle, a set of narrow-bladed scissors, and a pair of pliers.
Usage Implications: Proficiency allows adding your bonus to ability checks to disarm traps or open locks.

Name: Tinderbox
Description: A small container holding flint, fire steel, and dry tinder.
Usage Implications: Used to light a torch, or start a small fire. Lighting a fire takes 1 action.

Name: Torch
Description: A wooden shaft tipped with oil-soaked rags.
Usage Implications: Burns for 1 hour. Casts bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch, it deals 1 fire damage.

Name: Waterskin
Description: A treated leather bag designed to hold drinking water.
Usage Implications: Holds up to 4 pints of liquid. Essential for surviving travel to avoid exhaustion from dehydration.

Name: Smokestick
Description: An alchemically treated wooden stick that instantly emits a thick cloud of obscuring smoke when broken or struck.
Usage Implications: As an action, creates a 10-foot-radius sphere of heavily obscured smoke that lasts for 1 minute or until dispersed by wind.

Name: Sunrod
Description: A metal rod tipped with an alchemical crystal that glows brightly when struck against a hard surface.
Usage Implications: Provides bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet. Glows continuously for 6 hours without producing heat or requiring oxygen.

Name: Tanglefoot Bag
Description: A fragile bladder filled with rapid-setting alchemical resin.
Usage Implications: Thrown as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target's movement speed is reduced to 0 until they use an action to pass a Strength check to break free.
